title: Feature request: pause/resume and amount changes for AMC SIPs on Coin
originalText:
Could the Coin team support pause/resume and permitted amount changes for AMC SIPs? The current [AMC SIP help page](https://support.zerodha.com/category/mutual-funds/features-on-coin/systematic-investment-plan/articles/amc-sip-on-coin) says they cannot be paused, modified or stepped up.

This matters when a scheme restricts lump-sum investments. Regular Coin SIPs are processed as lump-sum orders; Zerodha's [September 2020 SBI Small Cap notice](https://zerodha.com/marketintel/bulletin/267485/suspension-of-lumpsum-investments-in-sbi-small-cap-fund) explained why those investors needed AMC SIPs. I also found the [2024 explanation that Coin SIPs would be converted to AMC SIPs, with conversion handled manually](https://tradingqna.com/t/coin-sip-vs-amc-sip/127618). Please clarify how that process works today and how investors are notified.

Carnelian Small Cap Fund is a useful upcoming example. Its [SID, pp. 52–53](https://carnelianmf.com/api/documents/file/SID_%20Carnelian%20Small%20Cap%20Fund-1.pdf?prefix=documents%2F01a0c7ec-70f3-7059-a143-544f8e604e61) provides for restricting lump-sum inflows after AUM reaches ₹5,000 crore, while explicitly continuing both existing and new SIP registrations.

Its [SAI, p. 90](https://carnelianmf.com/api/documents/file/SAI%20-%20Carnelian%20Mutual%20Fund.pdf?prefix=documents%2F01a0c7ec-70f3-7059-a143-544f8e604e61) expressly provides a pause facility for SIPs registered through BSE StAR MF. For monthly SIPs, it allows up to three instalments per pause, with at least 10 calendar days' notice and automatic restart. That makes it worth asking whether Coin can expose the facility and what integration or registration constraints remain.

The requests are:

1. **Pause and resume AMC SIPs** within the applicable AMC/platform rules, with eligibility and notice periods shown clearly.
2. **Amount changes and step-up where supported**, including top-up selection at registration where required. Explain when cancellation and re-registration are necessary.
3. **A clear conversion process when lump-sum investments are restricted:** whether the investor must act, how long conversion takes, and what happens to upcoming instalments.
4. **An upfront warning for documented restriction triggers**, explaining the implications of choosing a regular Coin SIP versus an AMC SIP.

The broader concern is being able to take a permitted pause without cancelling an existing registration. If a scheme later stops new SIP registrations, cancellation and re-registration may no longer be an option; Carnelian's current ₹5,000 crore provision does allow new registrations.

Could the Coin team consider these changes and explain any remaining AMC, BSE or Coin constraints?

title: Does making SIP only during market correction generates higher returns?
originalText:
Every time after I make a SIP investment, market tends to go down in next couple of days. I always wondered I would have made higher returns with my SIP if I waited for market correction. Momentum traders always get into a trade when there is a uptrend and exit their trades when the downtrend starts, even they think their SIP returns would have been higher if they invested only during market uptrend and avoid SIP during market downtrend to avoid major drawdowns.

Every one of us would have thought about it, we always assume we might end up with higher SIP returns if we apply any specific strategy towards it.

Does making SIP only during market correction generates higher returns?

Let’s look at the historical chart of Nifty 50 for the last 16 years. Nifty has moved from 3000 odd levels in 2006 to 18000 levels by 2022. I have applied 10 month moving average to the chart, instead of using 200 day moving average I always prefer using 10 MA on monthly chart, because it greatly reduces the noise. When you use daily charts, there are lot of movements and tons of gaps that affects the over all trend when you apply a moving average chart into a daily charts, but once we move to monthly many of these noise are eliminated and shows a smooth graph which helps us to identify those bear markets.

When ever Nifty goes below 10 month moving average, we can consider the market has become weak and if goes above this 10 MA, then we can consider market has become strong. Let us consider different scenario for making our SIP investment on Index.

![](https://telegra.ph/file/a91011ce611b4094f305c.png)

1. Invest X amount only when market trades above 10 MA, if it close below 10MA on a monthly basis, then exit all our holdings. Wait for the index to close above 10 MA, once it does then invest all our investments again along with that will continue our monthly X SIP investment.
2. Invest X amount when market trades below 10 MA, if it close below 10MA on a monthly basis, then ONLY we will start our SIP, if markets continues to trade above 10MA, then we will continue to accumulate cash and wait for market crash, the movement it goes below 10 MA, then we will invest lumpsum of all savings we accumulated so far and also continue to invest X amount every month as long as it trades below 10 MA. The moment it goes above 10 MA, we will stop our investments and continue to accumulate cash.

Basically one scenario is follow momentum / trend following approach, where we invest only when market keeps going up and avoid investing during bear markets. Another approach is the most interesting one as many of us want to invest only during crash, where we keep investing during down trend alone and stay out of market and keep accumulating cash to invest for next crash.

Let’s see how much each of these approach would have returned if we followed it since 2006 to till date.

**Invest only during crash:**

Let’s consider the third scenario first, what would be our returns if invested only when market close below 10 MA. In last 16 years, there are 6 to 7 instances where market corrected significantly. In 2008, due to global financial crisis, market corrected more than 60% and again in 2016 due to Brexit /demonetisation and other geo political events Index corrected more than 20%, similarly in 2020 due to Corona pandemic market corrected around 30%. Our investing during crash approach would have made use of all these correction period and invested in index.

![](https://telegra.ph/file/cb0d369ef2c4196011595.png)

From Jan 2006 to Feb 2008, we would have not invested a single penny in markets, since Nifty continued to trade above 10 MA, so during these period we would have kept on accumulating cash, so consider if we are planning SIP investment of 1 lac every month, then for 26 months we would have just accumulated cash and deployed all that cash of 26 lacs in March 2008 when market closed below 10 MA, then until it moved above 10 MA, we would have continued our 1 lac sip investment to index every month and continued till April 2009, during the prolonged down move where index corrected 60%, we would have accumulated 894 units of Nifty index.

![](https://telegra.ph/file/913a26845278b07b3053e.png)

Like wise we replicate this from 2006 to 2022, with this approach we would have invested **1.98 crores so far and the fund value would be 4.57 Crores.**

**Invest during momentum:**

In this second approach, we are investing same SIP 1 lac every month only when market trades above 10 month moving average. We are investing only during up move and book all profits when down trend starts, and then re invest again when the up move resumes.

![](https://telegra.ph/file/d2e44442e459cb3fd815d.png)

From Jan 2006 to Feb 2008, we would have kept on investing every single month then booked all profits by march 2008 when market started its downtrend by closing below 10 MA.

![](https://telegra.ph/file/184cbeeaeacffcc9d8dc8.png)

With this approach we would have invested 26 lacs between jan 2006 to Feb 2009 and also made around 5 lacs profit since market also moved from 3000 to 6000 during this period. We will sell all our holdings in march 2008 when it closed below 10 month moving average. Then from march 2008 to April 2009 market was in heavy downtrend and it remained below 10 month moving average, so we would have not invested any single penny during this period but we would have accumulated cash every month by April 2009 it closed above 10 MA. So we will deploy all our accumulated cash + previous exited holdings value in April 2009 when index resumed its uptrend.

![](https://telegra.ph/file/1cb44ab3077e0a3813fc9.png)

Like wise we will repeat this approach from 2006 to 2022, with this approach of making SIP investment only during uptrend we would have invested **1.98 crores so far and the fund value would be 4.13 Crores.**

Let’s see what’s the maximum drawdown in both the cases.

**Downtrend SIP Investing:**

The maximum drawdown is around -23% when you make your SIP investment during downtrend.

![](https://telegra.ph/file/f32ebf58a8e625e9c5a4f.png)

**Uptrend SIP Investing:**

The maximum drawdown is around -14% when you make your SIP investment during uptrend. The drawdown is relatively lower in this scenario because we completely book profits and stay away from bear markets or prolonged downtrend period, hence our investment value doesn’t go down.

![](https://telegra.ph/file/fbc14e46300c6e64b3434.png)

Let us bring in a third approach

**Invest every month:**

In this approach, we follow the boring method of regularly investing every month. No analysis. No worry about downtrend or uptrend. Just keep investing. To our surprise, this approach of regular SIP investment every month has given the highest returns compared to any other approach of investing during uptrend vs downtrend. With this approach we would have invested **1.98 crores so far and the fund value would be 4.88 Crores.**

![](https://telegra.ph/file/373808665b13f6b15af39.png)

Even the drawdowns with normal SIP is around -23% only

![](https://telegra.ph/file/b4dda180474cac8d64f9d.png)

**Conclusion**:

Market always tends to go up in the long run since economy of most of the countries might face short term pressures but over the larger period due to rise in working population, the economy does well which in turn reflects in stock market. We can never be sure about any single company, so betting our savings through SIP on stock specific might be riskier, instead investing in index funds is comparatively less risker. Since the exchange keeps adding good performers to the index and keeps removing bad ones from the index, this ensures smooth upward journey in index move.

By testing our SIP investing approach in both scenarios uptrend and downtrend, we can conclude that the regular boring approach beats every other type of investing strategy.

Just keep investing!

title: Feature Request - Coin: Flexible SIP Execution & Skip Option (+ Bulk Actions)
originalText:
Hello Team,

I’d like to suggest an enhancement to the SIP functionality that would give investors more flexibility and ease of use.

**Use Case:**
SIPs are executed automatically on their scheduled date, as they should (e.g., the 28th of each month). However, there are scenarios where I may see a market opportunity and prefer to execute my SIP earlier; for example, on August 14th instead of waiting until the 28th.

**Proposed Feature:**

* Add an **“Execute Now”** option for the SIP.
* While executing early, provide a **checkbox/option to skip the upcoming scheduled execution** (to avoid double execution for the same month).

**Extended Request (Bulk Actions):**

* A **bulk option** to apply “Execute Now” or “Skip This Month” across multiple SIPs at once.
* Similarly, a **bulk reschedule option** to adjust SIP dates, rather than editing them one by one.

**Current Workaround:**
Right now, the only way to handle this is by editing each SIP and backdating it so it won’t trigger again this month, then placing my order manually, which is quite time-consuming.

This feature would make SIP investing more convenient, especially for investors managing multiple SIPs.

Thanks for considering this!

title: Redeem or Continue? Clear your SIP doubts
originalText:
The lockdown may have impacted your investments.

In hindsight, the market crash was nothing more than a bump in the long journey to wealth creation.

Today we discuss why this time is as good as any other to kick start your SIP engine to life.

Yes, it's not too late!

It is certainly possible to revive your financial goals, [regardless of any market situation](https://www.quantumamc.com/investor-education/quantum-direct/how-to-grow-your-wealth-during-a-pandemic/qd-2197).

So here we present our SIP prescription for you to accumulate wealth for your financial goals.

#### I'm facing a threat to my income? What should I do?

Job losses, and salary or business income cuts have pushed many to rethink their SIPs.

Of course if you have any of the above problems, your primary focus should be on ensuring your emergency corpus is solid.

Shore up your corpus such that you have at least 12-18 months' worth of living expenses.

If you have planned well, then still try and continue your SIPs by cutting your expenses.

If not, once you have an emergency corpus in place, resume your SIPs to accumulate wealth for your financial goals.

#### I am facing a minor income cut, should I be worried?

It's great if you have faced little or no change in your income. In this case there is no reason that you shouldn't continue your SIPS as before.

In fact, given the opportunities around, you could consider cutting back on expenses and squeezing out extra cash for another SIP.

If your portfolio is exposed only to equity mutual funds, then consider adding some liquid funds. This will diversify your portfolio and allow you to raise money for short term goals.

Gold is a popular choice when it comes to diversifying portfolios. During times of market volatility gold prices generally go up when the markets are down. Consider allocating [10-15% of your portfolio to Gold](https://www.quantumamc.com/investor-education/quantum-direct/q-a-on-gold-with-our-fund-manager-chirag-mehta/qd-2194).

#### This volatility is unsettling, what should I do?

It's true that volatility in recent years has tested investors' patience.

But this doesn't imply that you should stop or redeem your SIPs. Remember that patience and tenacity are the hallmarks of wealth creation.

A better course of action would be to keep your expectations in check.

In a down market, expecting higher returns will only demotivate you.

And if you are invested in SIPs, you don't need to time markets or decide every month where to invest.

Simply continue your SIPs as before.

Continuing your SIPs at the same level means buying more units when markets are down. This also brings down your cost of acquisition.

#### What should I do if my goals have not changed and I have enough time?

For example let's say you have 7 to 10 years to achieve your goal. In this case, allow the portfolio to recover its value, and don't disturb your SIPs.

Holding on to your nerves is difficult when you see markets slipping to new lows.

The very action of committing to an SIP removes the need to identify market peaks and bottoms.

It also gives your portfolio the chance to benefit from the volatility.

#### I really need money urgently. Should I redeem my SIPs?

Consider redeeming investments in falling markets only in truly extreme situations.

Even if you have no choice but to redeem, consider all other options first.

In conclusion, to be able to reap benefits when markets do recover, it is important to remain invested.

title: Introducing updated Stock SIP experience on Kite web
originalText:
The Stock SIP on Kite has been updated to offer a more streamlined, intuitive experience, featuring a simplified creation process and new investment options.

**Process Improvements**

The requirement to create a basket before starting a SIP has been removed. The updated process allows for the direct addition of instruments upon initiating a new SIP, eliminating additional steps.

**Creation and Setup of Stock SIP**

* **Initiation:** Access via Orders > SIP > Click on New SIP,
or
via Marketwatch > More Options > Start SIP.

  The default name, "My SIP," can be customized.

* **Scheduling:** Frequencies include Monthly, Weekly, and Daily. Users may define the number of instalments (Until Cancelled, 6, 12, 24, 36, or custom).
![image|588x500, 75%](upload://c1qkgjv6pVnEv5fk9teqoB8XV9p.png)


* **SIP type:**

  * **Amount-based SIPs:** Selecting this mode automatically assigns the quantity based on the investment amount. Estimated quantities and amounts are displayed, and total amounts or individual instrument weights can be customized. There is a 'Split equally' option to automatically distribute the total investment amount evenly across all stocks in your basket. Additionally, the 'Lock' feature allows to freeze the weightage of specific instruments, ensuring those allocations remain unchanged even if the overall investment amount is adjusted.
![SIP_amount_lock_video|690x342](upload://bj3YOw3uyi4D6TPjyKSMIWkyknK.gif)

  * **Quantity-based SIPs:** This mode allows setting up SIP based on stock quantities.
![image|638x500, 75%](upload://t2omXeizupj5BUX1i0jIYJIkl8p.png)


* **Payment Modes:**
  * **Fund Balance:** Utilizes funds available in the trading account. Sufficient funds need to be maintained by the SIP date.
  * **UPI Autopay:** Facilitates automated payments directly from a linked bank account. Setup involves entering a mandate name, UPI ID, and accepting terms.
![image|554x500, 75%](upload://fep7MJBQ2nCOeS5JB0N6v84rddm.png)


**Modification of Stock SIP**

SIPs can be modified by selecting the specific SIP or choosing "Edit" from the options menu. Modifications can be made to frequency, date, time, number of installments, or payment modes. Price and quantity adjustments are managed within the order window for specific instruments.

Additionally, options to Pause, Resume, Skip the next installment, or delete the SIP are available in the options menu.

![SIP_modify_video|690x342](upload://yyS5iqCR1mMqBGffc1Jokfm6JWq.gif)


**Important Considerations**

* **Autopay Mandate:** Enabling the amount-based investment mode requires the configuration of an Autopay mandate. Autopay debits occur one day before each instalment.
* **Amount Defaults:** Amount-based SIPs default to a total of Rs. 5,000, which is fully customizable.
* **Execution:** Market orders with market protection are applied by default. The order type can be switched to Limit, but the execution is not guaranteed. Daily SIPs are executed between Monday and Friday. Monthly SIPs falling on a trading holiday are executed on the next available trading day.
* **Instalments**: Once the selected number of instalments is reached, the SIP status updates to "Completed."
* **Legacy SIPs:** SIPs created before this update remain unaffected and will continue to execute according to their original schedule. However, modifications are not permitted for existing SIPs with multiple schedules. To make changes, any extra schedules must be removed first.
![image|489x500](upload://n6jhdkm4RZvSW0w44ubt3ndjrtZ.png)

* **Availability and Transition:** This feature is currently available on Kite Web and will be introduced to the mobile app shortly. During this rollout, SIPs created on the Web open a basket view when accessed. Please note that during this transition, modifications are permitted for Monthly SIPs but not for Daily or Weekly SIPs.
![ScreenRecording_SIP_Goal|242x500](upload://JrIEci91rH5rjV8lLgz46EYDmh.gif)
